intro: Fast food and counter work builds coordination, service and people-reading skills that kitchens, stores and offices all use. Of the 25 careers below, Dining Room and Cafeteria Attendants match best at 91%, and 23 of the 25 pay more than the $31,200 median.
why_it_works: A fast food shift means taking orders fast, keeping the line moving and staying calm when customers are upset. O*NET rates coordination, service orientation and social perceptiveness at 3 out of 5 for this job, so cook, cashier and clerk roles rank high. Moving to the kitchen or into stock work keeps the pace you know with different tasks. Supervisor and manager roles build on the teamwork you use every rush. The skills to add include quality control and troubleshooting.
tips: Ask for shift lead training, since Food Service Managers pay more than double the fast food median.
Write down what you handle in a shift, such as orders, cash and new staff you trained, and put it on your resume.
Try a cook or prep role if you like the pace but want higher pay without a degree.

faq.q: What jobs can fast food workers do next?
faq.a: The closest matches are Dining Room and Cafeteria Attendants and Bartender Helpers (91%), Cooks, Fast Food (86%) and Food Preparation Workers (83%), based on O*NET 31.0. Outside food service, Cashiers (80%) and Stockers and Order Fillers (79%) use the same speed and teamwork.

faq.q: Which jobs pay more than fast food?
faq.a: 23 of the 25 matches pay more than the $31,200 median for fast food and counter workers. Food Service Managers earn $69,390 (+122%), and Postal Service Clerks earn $62,130 (+99%), according to BLS May 2025 data. Butchers and Meat Cutters earn $40,140 (+29%).

faq.q: Can I leave fast food without a degree?
faq.a: Yes. All 25 matches usually need no more education than a fast food job, based on O*NET Job Zones. Most of the training is on the job: the closest match usually takes up to 1 month to learn, and 74% of its workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent.

faq.q: What restaurant jobs are close to fast food work?
faq.a: If you want to stay in food service, the nearest roles are Waiters and Waitresses (90% match), Food Servers, Nonrestaurant (89%), Baristas (86%) and Bartenders (83%). These use the same customer skills in a different setting and pace.
